title: Data Visualization Fundamentals
subject: Data and Analytics
description: Choose the right chart for the question, use colour and labels clearly, avoid misleading charts, and design dashboards people can read at a glance.

lessons.title: Choosing the right chart
lessons.body:
The chart should follow from the question:

- **Comparison across categories:** bar chart, sorted by value.
- **Change over time:** line chart.
- **Part of a whole:** a stacked bar, or a pie chart only with two or three slices.
- **Distribution:** histogram or box plot.
- **Relationship between two measures:** scatter plot.

A table is often the right choice when the reader needs exact values. Ask 'What should the reader see first?' and pick the chart that makes that point obvious.

lessons.title: Honest and clear charts
lessons.body:
Several common choices mislead readers:

- **Truncated bar axes:** starting a bar chart above zero exaggerates differences. Bars should start at zero.
- **3D effects:** they distort the size of each part.
- **Inconsistent scales:** comparing charts that use different axis ranges without saying so.
- **Too many series:** a chart with eight coloured lines is hard to read. Highlight the one or two that matter.

Label the axes, state the units, and give each chart a title that says what it shows, not only what it is.

lessons.title: Colour, labels, and emphasis
lessons.body:
Use colour to highlight, not decorate. Grey out background categories and colour the one you want the reader to notice. Keep colour choices readable for colour-blind viewers, and do not rely on red and green alone to show good and bad.

Direct labels on the data are easier to read than a separate legend. Remove gridlines and borders that do not help the reader.

lessons.title: Designing a dashboard
lessons.body:
A dashboard should answer a small set of questions for a defined audience. Arrange it in order of importance: headline KPIs at the top, supporting trends below, and detail at the bottom or on a separate page.

Test the dashboard by asking a colleague to find the answer to a common question within 30 seconds. If they cannot, simplify it.

questions.text: Which chart best shows change over time?
Why should bar charts usually start at zero?
What is the best use of colour in a chart?
options: To highlight the one or two things the reader should notice
To match the company logo only
correct: To highlight the one or two things the reader should notice

questions.text: Which are misleading or unclear chart practices? (Select all that apply)
options: 3D effects that distort the size of parts
Eight coloured lines with no highlighting
correct: 3D effects that distort the size of parts
Eight coloured lines with no highlighting

questions.text: On a dashboard, headline KPIs should appear at the top.
